concepts_in_source_text_not_in_dataset: אֵשׁ (the primordial fire from birth) — not a formal bechina term but the central structural concept: all desires are fueled by it. No bechina edge encoded for ref=253. If this teaching were to be encoded, אֵשׁ would be the dominant node of a neutral/evil structural package together with תַּאֲוַת נִאוּף.

תַּאֲוַת נִאוּף / תַּאֲוַת הַמִּשְׁגָּל — the text uses both terms interchangeably for the same desire, implying they share the same essential nature (a potential bechina). No edge encoded for ref=253.

מֹחַ (brain/mind) — appears as a structural concept damaged by sleep extremes. In other Torahs (e.g., #29: מחין) the brain is a major node. For ref=253 it has only an eitza relationship (sleep damages the brain), not an explicit bechina.

שֵׁנָה (sleep) — appears in both its reduced and excessive forms; both have an eitza relationship (cause-effect) to the fire. In Torah #29, שנה is bechina of מחין דקטנות — but that bechina language is absent here.
תַּבְעֵרוֹת שֶׁל כָּל הַתַּאֲווֹת (burning desire of all lusts) — the general category of desire produced by the fire; eitza relationship only.
גּוּף (body) — the body receives food and drink which the fire burns; purely structural/eitza context.
אֲכִילָה וּשְׁתִיָּה (eating and drinking) — consumed by the fire; eitza context only.
גִּבּוֹר / כִּבּוּשׁ הַיֵּצֶר (warrior / conquering the inclination) — the practical conclusion: no eitza helps, only heroic inner conquest. This is a moral exhortation, not a bechina statement.
analysis_notes.encoding_recommendation: Torah #253 is a short oral teaching (שִׂיחָה) reported by Reb Noson with the caveat that the Rebbe's full intention was not clearly stated. The teaching describes a physiological-spiritual mechanism using exclusively causal language. Before encoding bechina edges for this Torah, a careful review of whether any relationships cross the bechina/eitza boundary is required. The most credible bechina candidate is: אֵשׁ (primordial fire) ↔ תַּאֲוַת נִאוּף — as both are presented as aspects of the same destructive inner reality fueled by the body's natural constitution. The practical takeaway (strengthen yourself to be a 'gibbor') aligns this Torah with a broader יֵצֶר הָרָע cluster found in other Torahs, but no formal bechina encoding can be proposed from this text alone without risking incorrect classification of eitza chains as bechina pairs.
